events.title: Hungarian Revolution Begins
events.description: Students and citizens in Budapest began a large demonstration that turned into a nationwide uprising against the Soviet-backed communist government and Soviet domination of Hungary. Soviet forces intervened on November 4 and crushed the revolt.
events.significance: The uprising was one of the first major challenges to Soviet control in Eastern Europe. It exposed the limits of de-Stalinization and shaped Cold War politics and Western perceptions of the USSR.

events.title: Second Battle of El Alamein Begins
events.description: British Eighth Army forces under General Bernard Montgomery launched a massive artillery barrage and offensive against Axis forces led by Erwin Rommel at El Alamein in Egypt.
events.significance: The British victory marked a turning point in the North African Campaign. It ended the Axis threat to Egypt and the Suez Canal and boosted Allied morale.

events.title: Beirut Barracks Bombings
events.description: Two truck bombs struck the U.S. Marine barracks and a French paratrooper building in Beirut, Lebanon, killing 241 American and 58 French servicemen during the Lebanese Civil War.
events.significance: It was the deadliest single-day loss of U.S. Marines since Iwo Jima. The attacks led to the withdrawal of the multinational peacekeeping force from Lebanon and influenced later U.S. counterterrorism policy.

events.title: Hungary Proclaims the Republic
events.description: Hungary formally declared itself the Republic of Hungary, replacing the People's Republic and adopting constitutional changes that allowed multiparty democracy and free elections.
events.significance: The proclamation was a landmark in the peaceful end of communist rule in Central Europe during the revolutions of 1989, occurring on the anniversary of the 1956 uprising.

events.title: First Parliament of Great Britain Meets
events.description: The first Parliament of Great Britain convened, combining the English and Scottish parliaments after the Acts of Union took effect earlier that year.
events.significance: It established the unified legislature of the Kingdom of Great Britain, laying the foundation for the modern British parliamentary system.
